aero.air_density_note: ISA sea-level standard value. Kept at Level 1 by convention like wheelbase_m -- not a sourced-vs-placeholder distinction, a fixed physical constant that would only move for a session weather correction (not implemented).
aero.lift_coeff_sign_convention: cl < 0 means downforce, cl > 0 means lift (standard aero Cl sign; NOT a downforce-positive convention) -- CONFIRMED computationally 2026-08-30 against the live estimate_vertical_loads code, not just inferred from the formula. thesis_notes.md 'Aero downforce sign convention verified computationally'. The FIRST real Cl entry must be negative.
aero.lift_coeff_note: Sign convention verified against the chair's own formula (docs/literature/data_handler.py:1559, fz_aero_total_N = -0.5*rho*v^2*A*Cl, commented 'positive for downforce'): since -0.5*rho*v^2*A is never positive, Cl must be NEGATIVE for a downforce-generating car under this convention -- standard aerodynamic lift-coefficient sign (positive=lift, negative=downforce), not a 'downforce coefficient' convention where downforce would read positive. No numeric Cl default exists in the shared reference files to confirm against directly; this is inferred from the formula+comment pairing alone, not an assumed value. Placeholder 0.0: the aero term evaluates to exactly zero at every speed, i.e. Fz reduces to the static+longitudinal-only estimate -- a documented underestimate of both axles' load at speed, not a front/rear balance error. When populated with a real (negative) Cl, re-verify sign against a high-speed straight-line sample (fz_f_N+fz_r_N should exceed the static sum, not fall below it). This sign convention is INFERRED from the formula+comment pairing, not confirmed against a real value -- the first real Cl entry must be validated empirically (Fz increasing with v^2, not decreasing) before being trusted.
aero.cross_track_area_note: Not sourced -- inert while lift_coeff=0.0 (multiplies to zero regardless). Must be sourced together with a real lift_coeff before either has a numeric effect.
aero.diff_cog_x_note: CoP-to-CoG longitudinal offset. Not sourced, inert while lift_coeff=0.0. 0.0 also has a standalone physical meaning if ever populated alone: aero centre of pressure coincides with CoG, i.e. no front/rear aero balance shift.

stability_estimation._comment_yaw_rate_unit: The unit yaw_rate_to_radps converts from (rpm: 2*pi/60 = 0.10472). 2026-10-17 (Class B #5/#6): checked against the file's declared sclu_yaw_rate unit in csv_parser._assert_fixed_factor_units; a mismatch stops the parse instead of scaling yaw rate by the wrong factor.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: CS window floors: cs_min_window_s = 0.1 s, the chair's own value, unchanged. Tested 0.2 s against it on real data (100 Hz grid): same results on all 14 corners, no bootstrap difference -> no reason to deviate. Bootstrap spread measures precision, not closeness to the true tangent; floors chosen by direct validation.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py + inspect_cs_duration_only_comparison.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Exactly the chair's own literal default (10 samples @ their 100 Hz = 0.1s), zero deviation, now that the 100 Hz grid supplies the sample count that default always assumed. A 0.2s hypothesis (double the chair's value, motivated by an a priori 'this car's alpha comes from an ESTIMATED beta -- kinematic or EKF/auto-fit, a noisier Level 1-3 chain -- vs the chair's own MEASURED beta channel, so more averaging seemed plausible') was TESTED AND REJECTED, not just superseded: an isolated duration-only bootstrap (span held at 0.02 rad, cornering-only population) found 0.1s and 0.2s statistically indistinguishable at every tested phase length, and direct real-data validation confirmed the two floors reproduce the SAME worst-lap population almost exactly (identical negative-corner counts, same corners flagged, C4 rear even reads a stronger negative at 0.1s). The plausible-sounding physical story was not supported by either form of evidence gathered -- recorded honestly rather than left implied.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.2s*20Hz=4 samples would round below a robust minimum; floored at 5 (same magnitude as cs_phase_min_valid_samples's own robustness reasoning), mirroring modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own min_samples_floor precedent.
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Rate-independent (alpha-domain, radians) -- no sample-rate correction applies. Reverted from attempt 2's falsified 0.01 rad back to 0.02 rad (the chair's own original span) after direct real-data validation; unaffected by the separate cs_min_window_s duration question (0.2s vs 0.1s) -- span was never the axis in question there.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: Locality cap for CS window growth, in track metres (state['s_m']), not samples -- same meaning in slow and fast corners. Natural window on corner samples: median 24.1 m front / 35.4 m rear (diagnostics/inspect_cs_max_window_locality_sizing.py); cap = 1.5 x rear median = 53 m. No corner lost at either floor (diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py). The span floor, not min_window, sets the real window size. Limitation: some corner-to-corner gaps are < 53 m, so a window can bridge into a neighbour there. Floors not met within the cap -> NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: Per-phase CS_ratio median -> NaN below this many finite samples. 5 = smallest n where the median isn't just one or two extreme readings. Generic backstop; apex_3 handled by apex_region.
stability_estimation._comment_ls_phase_min_valid_samples: Same gate for ls_ratio_f/r, own key (LS noise differs from CS). Same criterion, same value.
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: entry_1_brake stability stat: same sample-count gate as CS (cs_phase_min_valid_samples), plus no signal if max brake_f_bar never exceeds this floor (no real braking). v3 log_pbrake_f at throttle > 90%: 32829 samples, p99 = 0 bar, one 6.03 bar transient (diagnostics/inspect_v3_brake_phase_stability.py). Real braking phases >= 13.6 bar. 3.0 bar sits between.
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: diagnostics/inspect_cs_window_floor_derivation.py, linear_region_end, 2026-09-02 (CS validity repair). Binned the session's own Fy-vs-alpha cloud (both axles, folded to a single sign via the tyre curve's expected odd symmetry, moving & non-kerb samples) with sliding 0.04-rad-wide windows (matched to the re-derived cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad, not an arbitrary narrow bin -- a narrower bin reproduces the same small-span sampling noise the N/span sweeps diagnosed) stepped by 0.005 rad, comparing each window's local slope against the near-origin reference window ([0,0.04) rad). Departure stays within +/-15% of the reference out to ~0.03 rad on both axles, then exceeds 10% and STAYS exceeded (not a single noisy crossing) from window leading edge 0.045 rad (front) / 0.035 rad (rear) onward, climbing to full sign reversal by ~0.08-0.09 rad -- the genuine nonlinear/saturation region. Value set at the more conservative (earlier-onset) axle's sustained-departure point, 0.035 rad, rounded down slightly to 0.03 rad for a safety margin against measurement noise; both axles' own curves are still flat (within a few % of the reference) at 0.03 rad.
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: Common grid = min(target_sample_rate_hz, slowest native rate of the fast CS channels: sclu_yaw_rate, log_asteer, log_acc_y, log_acc_z, lap_distance). On Dubai those are 100 Hz, ecu_speed 50 Hz (diagnostics/inspect_native_channel_rates.py); ecu_speed upsampled linearly (inertia-limited). Below min_sample_rate_hz -> refused, naming the binding channel; exactly 50 Hz -> runs, status 'channel-limited'. Windows are durations converted at the grid rate (kerb_dilation_s, kerb_smear_grade_s, cs_min_window_s, nis_window_s in tyre_fit_auto and nis_gate, yaw_stability_accel_window_s); the EKF Q is scaled to the grid step (tyre_fit_auto.q_reference_rate_hz). Known limit: apex_half_window_samples is still a sample count (+/-0.05 s at 100 Hz). [History, 2026-10-17 (R6 docs cycle): this comment listed as known limits the Dugoff pass_1 R calibrated on the old 50 Hz grid and the nis_window_samples keys (nis_gate / tyre_fit_auto / tyre_model_ekf); the NIS windows became durations (nis_gate 2026-09-03, tyre_fit_auto 2026-10-16), and tyre_model_ekf and the remaining nis_window_samples key were removed with the Dugoff path (2026-10-17).] [2026-10-03: kerb_dilation_samples removed from this list -- replaced by the time-based kerb_dilation_s (Q-CAL-1 option 0).]
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: Which beta feeds Modules 4b/5. Default 'ekf_auto_pacejka' (per-session fit, gated, kinematic fallback). 'kinematic' = estimate_sideslip, the universal fallback. [2026-10-17: 'ekf_pass_1' (frozen Dugoff curve) removed with the Dugoff path; any other value now stops the run instead of silently running kinematic.] Traces are fine under any source; verdict thresholds are calibrated for thresholds_calibrated_for_sideslip_source only -> [UNCAL] banner otherwise.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source_auto_modes: 'ekf_auto_pacejka': fit this session's tyre curve (tyre_fit_auto), run the NIS gate, use the EKF's beta_with_fallback only if gate = pass/warn and fit not degenerate; else kinematic, recorded as fallback_used/fallback_reason. Thresholds are never calibrated for these -> [UNCAL] always. [2026-10-17: 'ekf_auto_dugoff' removed with the Dugoff path (it fell back to kinematic on every run on this car).]
stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: 'static' = estimate_vertical_loads' static/aero/transfer model. 'measured' = wheel_loads cascade (damper -> axle-total reconstruction -> static) for the Fz used by fy_norm and the tyre fit. No damper channels (e.g. Dubai) -> every corner invalid -> cascade returns static everywhere, identical by construction.
stability_estimation.vertical_load_source_derived_from: DEFAULT FLIPPED to 'measured' 2026-09-04 (user decision) -- verdict independence PROVEN, not assumed, before the flip: CS_ratio/stability (the only classification/verdict inputs) never receive fz as an argument at all (code-level: estimate_cornering_stiffness/estimate_yaw_moment_stability's own signatures) and both run BEFORE fz is computed in the pipeline; empirically confirmed on Dubai -- fz_f_N differed by up to 8591.8N between static and measured, but CS_ratio_f/CS_ratio_r/C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r/stability_observed_Nm_per_deg were BYTE-IDENTICAL. The flip therefore carries ZERO classification/verdict risk by construction -- it only changes fy_f_norm_N/fy_r_norm_N (display) and the Phase-2 diagnostic mu tyre-fit's own load input, both display/diagnostic quantities. tests/test_vertical_load_source_default.py confirms the live default is 'measured' and resolves correctly both with real damper channels present (measured cascade engages, every corner tier=damper) and without any (falls back automatically, numerically identical to an explicit 'static' run).
stability_estimation._comment_gps_course_anchor: estimate_sideslip_gps (validation only) anchor gate: smoothed |ay| < max_ay_g for >= min_duration_s. Raw per-sample |ay| gave only ~0.1 s runs; smooth_window_s 0.3 -> 6 runs >= 1.5 s on Dubai. max_ay_g 0.05 ~ moving |ay| p10 (0.044 g), before the rise toward cornering (p20 0.109 g). diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py.
stability_estimation.gps_course_latency_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py (GPS-course sideslip validation, 2026-07-26): cross-correlation of wrap-safe d(course)/dt against -yaw_rate_radps over lags -1..+1s (racing laps, moving samples) peaks at r=0.9898 at lag=+0.32s, vs r=0.9575 at zero lag -- course-derived rotation consistently lags yaw_rate by this much. A stale course reading recorded at time t describes the vehicle's true state at (t - latency); querying it at (t + latency) recovers the value that actually corresponds to the query instant.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: apex_3 = one instant +/- apex_half_window_samples (11 samples; one helper, stability_analysis.apex_instant_slice, for every consumer -- corner statistics, tyre-fit h2 check, TPMS apex read-out -- always this width since 2026-10-17) -- can't clear the CS window floor. apex_region = +/- cs_apex_region_half_length_m around the apex position, used for apex_3 CS reads in classification; apex_3 unchanged otherwise. 25 m = half the ~20-40 m extent of the C4 CS dip -> inside one event, short of the next straight or corner.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); values = the chair's defaults. Changing any of the six means re-deriving the classification thresholds.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback C_linear_ref: axle load x C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 (Milliken RCVD, GT3 slick). Front (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268, rear (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Level 1. Only used as the fixed stiffness prior of diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py; no production consumer. [2026-10-03 CORRECTION, text only, no value change (PLAN.md section 7 note 7b, Q-PUSH exit ruling 1): the same C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 on both axles implies a NEUTRAL-STEER car (K = 0). The measured understeer gradient is K2 = +1.27 to +1.41 deg/g (understeer; Q-PUSH P1, Rajamani Eq. 3.23 regression, three sessions) -- named as the measured replacement candidate (Q-K2).] [2026-10-17: the understeer-gradient (K) readout is removed from the application (author decision; basis as stated by the author: Guiggiani 2023, K not meaningful with significant downforce), so the Q-K2 replacement candidate is void; this value stays a diagnostics-only prior.]
stability_estimation.kerb_dilation_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 0, author ruling 2026-10-03 (neutral engineering, unit repair). Replaces kerb_dilation_samples = 5, which was set as 100 ms each side on the old fixed 50 Hz grid and silently ran as +/-50 ms after the grid moved to 100 Hz (formerly a known limit in _comment_grid_rate). Restores the calibrated +/-100 ms; samples = round(kerb_dilation_s x grid rate) at runtime, so the physical padding is the same at 50 and 100 Hz. Premise check: diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py, thesis_notes 'Q-CAL-1 measurement'.
stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 4, author rulings 2026-10-03. Grade-zone width of the near_strike mark: a CS window [start, i) holding a sample within this time of a kerb-mask sample (outside the mask, either side), or a mask sample itself (R1, 2026-10-17), carries the mark. Marked samples are left out of the per-phase CS verdict statistics (since schema 12, 2026-10-05); the CS arrays keep them. The zone also bars a window from setting the CS linear reference (Fix 0, 2026-10-17) and is excluded from the tyre-fit base mask with the kerb mask (R6, 2026-10-17). [Corrected 2026-10-17 (R6 docs cycle): the text read 'Flag only -- no exclusion, no down-rank, no verdict change', the rule of 2026-10-03.] The 2 Hz zero-phase CS filter runs before the mask and spreads a strike into unmasked neighbours; diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py measured the Fy smear past the edge at p75 = 0.25 s (15 NBR + 2 Paul Ricard sessions) and the coincidence count shows the deep-CS enrichment ending there (rear ends ~250 ms; front 250-360 ms band adds only x1.7). GEOMETRY: that 0.25 s was measured from the OLD +/-50 ms mask edge; the restored +/-100 ms dilation (kerb_dilation_s) moves the edge out by 50 ms, so 0.20 s from the new edge keeps the same measured physical boundary. One value, both axles (no front/rear difference in the Fy smear). Tier B.

nis_gate.nis_window_s_derived_from: Bug fix, 2026-09-03. SUPERSEDES the literal window_samples=20 key (removed): that value was always a 50Hz-calibrated PHYSICAL duration (20/50=0.4s), silently treated as rate-independent -- once the 100Hz time base moved BOTH Dubai and any 100Hz session onto that grid, window_samples=20 silently represented only 0.2s, HALF its intended duration, for every session this gate has ever evaluated (rate-corrected, Dubai's health_score falls 0.1417->0.1351 and v3's falls 0.1163->0.0849). Same rate-derivation pattern as stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s (modules.stability_analysis.resolve_cs_min_window_samples) and modules.nis_gate.resolve_nis_window_samples now derives the effective sample count from THIS file's own measured sample_rate_hz at runtime, so the window can never again silently mean a different duration on a different grid rate. threshold_use_ekf/threshold_warn are UNCHANGED by this fix -- the band/threshold decision is recorded in threshold_derived_from.
nis_gate.threshold_derived_from: RE-DERIVED 2026-10-11 (phase 2 step 2 Part 3, same recorded rule as 2026-09-03 below, on the corrected estimator at the ruled R picks; diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py --step p2s2robust): health scores of eight real sessions -- Dubai 0.0549, PR MLA outing 25 0.0473, PR MLA outing 32 0.0245, NBR JST 21 0.0663, NBR JST 29 0.0995, NBR qualifying CDR 0.1026, NBR qualifying MLA 0.0795, NBR-73-010-026-JDR 0.1219. The distribution moved down (under the old values five of the seven pool sessions would read 'warn'): the combined NIS now carries the yaw model mismatch exposed by the honest re-entry. threshold_use_ekf = 0.023, a round number about 6 % below the lowest real score (PR outing 32, 0.0245), so every real session lands in PASS; threshold_warn = 0.0025, about an order of magnitude below that lowest score, reserved for a collapsed fit. Level 1 calibration tunables. Supersedes 0.08 / 0.01. [Previous text:] NIS gate band decision, 2026-09-03: divergence, not quality. SUPERSEDES the five-synthetic-data-point gap-selection above (threshold_use_ekf=0.1385/threshold_warn=0.1006): at n=2 real sessions (Dubai, GT3_PRC_MLA-v3) the gate cannot grade fit QUALITY -- there is not enough evidence to say one healthy session's score is 'better' than another's -- so its job is redefined as catching DIVERGENCE only. threshold_use_ekf=0.08 is a round number set below the lower of the two real, live rate-corrected health scores (v3 0.084871, Dubai 0.135131, both re-measured via diagnostics/inspect_v3_nis_gate_failure.py) with a small safety margin (~6% below v3), so both real sessions land in PASS. threshold_warn=0.01 gap-selects the FAIL line roughly an order of magnitude below both real scores (8.5x below v3, 13.5x below Dubai) -- reserved for a genuinely collapsed fit (health_score near its structural floor of 0, meaning almost no rolling window ever lands in the healthy NIS-exceedance band), not ordinary session-to-session noise. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, not re-tested live (tests/test_nis_gate.py's synthetic-mismatch fixture is currently skipped for an unrelated reason, Dugoff degenerating on Dubai under the CS window floor): the synthetic mismatch scenario mu_fz_x2.0 (score 0.0674), which verdicted 'fail' under the old thresholds, would now verdict 'warn' -- an accepted trade-off of this redesign's own stated intent (real n=2 evidence over synthetic-scenario calibration), not an oversight. UPGRADE PATH: a chi-square consistency gate (Kiencke & Nielsen, Automotive Control Systems, 2nd ed. 2005 -- citation to verify) replaces this gap-selected band with a principled statistical test once its own noise-model caveat (R values are themselves gap-selected) is resolved or judged acceptable.

tyre_fit_auto.fit_speed_window_pct_derived_from: 2026-10-04, author ruling (session Step 2). Speed window on the Pacejka FIT POPULATION only (all three fit modes; NIS sweep, gate and CS keep the base mask): keep samples with speed inside [p_lo, p_hi] of the speed of moving samples inside corner instances on analysis laps, per session (self-adapting; fixed km/h rejected because it would mis-fit a track with a different speed envelope). null = off. Same function as the chair tyre fit's speed-band union (drops the fastest, mostly straight-line, near-zero-slip stretches); FORCED ADAPTATION -- one window instead of four band curves because the EKF consumes one signed curve per axle; the edge values are vehicle parameterisation. Tested in Q-FIT-DECISIVE as variant SW: verdict NEUTRAL; ships by AUTHOR OVERRULE (chair-closeness; pooled deep CS<-1 tail -40 %). Reference values, Tier-1 sessions: 69-70 to 222-229 km/h, 89-93 % of the base mask retained, 95-97 % of samples with |alpha_f| >= 1 deg retained, 2.0-2.1 % of in-corner fit samples dropped (diagnostics/inspect_speed_bands.py). tyre_fit_auto._comment_r_sweep_selection: Accuracy Level 1 calibration tunables (config default), Pacejka path (author ruling 2026-10-11). [2026-10-17: nis_band_low/high in this block were the removed Dugoff path's joint yaw + ay band; no estimator reads them, they stay only because diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py still prints them -- cleanup candidate.] R is selected on the ay NIS exceedance only: in [r_sweep_ay_band_low, r_sweep_ay_band_high], nearest the band centre, and only if that grid point's own sign-check fraction reaches sign_check_marginal_fraction; otherwise the next-nearest in-band point; none -> r_sweep_default_ay_scale / r_sweep_default_yaw_scale with status at most 'marginal' (marginal_reason r_sweep_no_in_band / r_sweep_guard_fail). Derivation: the full 25-point grid under the corrected divergence re-entry (diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py --step p2s2grid, run 2026-10-11) -- the yaw exceedance floor over the grid is 0.263 (Dubai), 0.211 (NBR-73-010-026-JDR), 0.393 (MLA-SE07_US-v2), far above any NIS band: the yaw innovation is dominated by single-track model mismatch, not sensor noise, so yaw is logged per point but not selected on. The ay exceedance reaches [0.03, 0.15] on all three exports, so the existing band limits are kept for ay. Default R = the setting the old sweep chose on all three exports (ay x0.1, yaw x16); the old 'nearest overall' pick is gone because it selected ay x1 / yaw x1 on Paul Ricard, where the sign check fell to 5/15.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_yaw_mismatch_ceiling: Accuracy Level 1 calibration tunable, Pacejka path only (author ruling 2026-10-11). The NIS gross-miscalibration trigger (nis_gross_miscalibration_fraction) reads the ay exceedance only; the yaw exceedance is logged per fit and can at most cap the status at 'marginal' (marginal_reason yaw_mismatch_high) when it exceeds this ceiling -- it never makes a fit degenerate. Under the honest re-entry the yaw NIS reflects single-track model mismatch, not noise calibration. Set well above the observed healthy yaw exceedance range (0.21-0.52 over the full R grid on Dubai, NBR-73-010-026-JDR and MLA-SE07_US-v2, grid run 2026-10-11) so it flags only anomalous sessions.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_status: ok/marginal/degenerate boundaries -- a proposal (status block of tyre_fit_auto.fit_session_pacejka; first stated in the removed Dugoff fit_session), not yet reviewed.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_load_normalised: load_normalised: fit D = mu * Fz with measured per-axle Fz (vertical_load_source 'measured') instead of a free D -> mu = peak friction coefficient (Milliken RCVD ch. 2 (sec. 2.1)). No measured Fz -> degenerate. load_normalised_fit_enabled gates it for 'ekf_auto_pacejka'; default false = free D. Not a production default.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_mu_plausibility_band: Plausible peak mu (D = mu*Fz) for a GT3 slick (Milliken RCVD, tyre chapter). Outside [low, high] -> flagged for the analyst, never silently kept or dropped.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_plausibility_gate: Tyre-curve plausibility gate (tyre_fit_auto.plausibility_gate, author decision 2026-10-07, D4). Accuracy Level 1 calibration tunables, per axle on the final fitted curve; any failed check routes the session into the existing degenerate-fit fallback (kinematic beta). Bands deliberately wide -- a garbage catch, not ridge adjudication. min_alpha_span_deg: p1..p99 span of the fit's slip-angle data (excitation). stiffness_min_npr / stiffness_max_npr: implied linear axle stiffness B*C*D in N/rad; magnitudes after Bechtloff (single-track reference values, Fig. 7.2) as coarse bounds. peak_min_deg / peak_max_deg: position of the curve's maximum; bracket around a team rule of thumb (front peak ~8 deg, personal communication, Proton race engineer) as a coarse bound.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_tyre_fit_mode: EXPERIMENTAL, config-selectable only (PLAN.md EXPERIMENT PLAN (d2), author ruling 2026-10-01). 'per_session' (production default): free four-parameter Pacejka fit per session from the chair start guess. 'prior_anchored': the same fit started from tyre_fit_prior and penalised by prior_weight * mean squared distance between session curve and prior curve over the session's visited slip range (Tikhonov regularisation towards a reference curve). Tier A anchor for a prior-plus-deviation tyre fit PENDING -- not a production default. Free D only: prior_anchored with load_normalised_fit_enabled true is refused as degenerate. Reading of prior_weight: the session's deviation from the prior shrinks by about 1 / (1 + w); 1 = medium (author ruling). (d2) result: under refit iteration the anchored fit converges only where the deviation is largely suppressed (thesis_notes.md (d2) entries).

tyre_fit_prior._comment: Pooled Pacejka prior (B, C, D [N], E) per axle: production _fit_axle_pacejka, unchanged, on the concatenated population of the 18 usable serial-221 sessions (kinematic alpha_f/r_filt, Fy_f/r_filt, _base_mask). Accuracy level 2 (pooled session measurement, kinematic-seeded). Dubai and Le Mans excluded (different tyres, logger 147). NBR carries 86.7 % of the samples -- not track-neutral. Refit only on a named event ((a3) shipping, tyre-spec change, author ruling), never on a new session.
tyre_fit_prior.derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_tyre_prior_d2.py prior, 2026-10-01; thesis_notes.md '(d2) Part 1: the mass-data prior'

longitudinal_stiffness._comment: LS_ratio: axle Fx and kappa (longitudinal_forces.py), windowed dFx/dkappa (longitudinal_stiffness.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal). cutoff_hz, linear_slip_threshold, min_speed_mps = chair defaults. min_window_s, min_window_samples_floor, min_slip_span, max_window_m = re-derived on this car's kappa/Fx, same adaptive-window scheme as CS (see each derived_from).
longitudinal_stiffness.rear_rolling_radius_offset_derived_from: Wheel-speed source characterization, 2026-08-18: rear axle (log_speed_rl/rr) reads a CONSTANT +1.41% high vs ecu_speed on straight-line samples, throttle-independent (median +1.44% on-throttle vs +1.41% overall) -- diagnosed as a rolling-radius difference, not traction slip. Corroborated independently by the GPS-speed cross-validation's k=1.01211 finding (same direction, unrelated measurement chain).
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_note: NOT sourced, placeholder -- same convention as vehicle.aero.lift_coeff. Inert regardless of this value while vehicle.aero.cross_track_area_m2 stays 0.0 (also not sourced); the fallback Fx tier's drag term evaluates to exactly zero, a documented underestimate, not a sign error.
longitudinal_stiffness.rolling_resistance_coeff_note: NOT sourced, placeholder. Unlike cog_height_m/track_width_m (which cannot legitimately be zero for a real car), zero rolling resistance is a defensible first-order racing-speed approximation on its own (rolling resistance is one to two orders of magnitude below aero drag and traction/braking forces at racing speed for a slick tyre) -- not an invented Tier A magnitude, a documented simplification, same epistemic move as lift_coeff=0.0.
longitudinal_stiffness.brake_front_fraction_fallback_note: Chair performance_analysis tooling's own default_brake_front_fraction constant (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py calculate_longitudinal_axle_forces, internal) -- adopted verbatim, used only when log_pbrake_f/log_pbrake_r are both unavailable/invalid (on this session's data both are whitelisted and valid, so the measured-split path is the one actually exercised).
longitudinal_stiffness.min_window_s_derived_from: LS validity repair, 2026-09-19, applying the CS_ratio validity-repair method -- SUPERSEDES regression_window_s (renamed: this is now a FLOOR the window adaptively widens past, not a fixed half-window). Method: bootstrap-resampled (B=150) phase-level MEDIAN stability (what summarise_corners's own _stats() actually feeds classify_fn/the frame) vs candidate (n,span), on real kappa/Fx, longitudinal-DEMAND population only (|ax|>1.0 m/s^2, moving, non-kerb), at the shortest MEANINGFUL representative corner-phase length per session (L=20 samples/0.2s -- the real p10 was 2-3 samples on both sessions, physically degenerate for ANY floor choice, excluded from governing the choice the same way CS excluded its own degenerate entry_1_brake case). GOVERNING case (smallest (n,span) clearing P75<=15% relative std, most demanding of 2 sessions x 2 axles): v3 rear axle, (n=40, span=0.016) -- median=0.044, P75=0.123 (diagnostics/inspect_ls_window_floor_derivation.py's own full grid: all other session/axle combinations clear at n<=40 too). 40 samples @ 100 Hz (both sessions' own resolved grid rate) = 0.40s -- notably close to the chair's own literal regression_window_s=0.45s default (a reassuring convergence, unlike CS's own bootstrap-vs-chair-literal tension that was later resolved in the chair's favour; no such tension here, the derived value and the chair's own choice already agree to within 0.05s).
longitudinal_stiffness.min_window_samples_floor_note: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.40s*20Hz=8 samples -- same reasoning as modules.stability_analysis's own cs_min_window_samples_floor (0.2s*20Hz=4, floored to 5); 8 needs no further rounding up since it already clears that same robustness bar. SUPERSEDES min_samples_floor=15 (the pre-repair 50 Hz half-window adaptation) -- that floor protected a DIFFERENT quantity (half_window+1 under a fixed, non-widening window) which no longer exists as a concept once the window adaptively widens past min_window_s.
longitudinal_stiffness.min_slip_span_derived_from: Same derivation run as min_window_s above (diagnostics/inspect_ls_window_floor_derivation.py) -- (n,span) chosen jointly, not independently, since the bootstrap tests the REAL adaptive-widening mechanism (reconstruct_ls_window_start) at each candidate pair. SUPERSEDES 0.004 (the chair's own literal LongitudinalStiffnessConfig.min_slip_span default, never re-derived for this car until now) -- a 4x increase, the same order-of-magnitude jump CS_ratio's own span floor needed (0.02->0.04 rad in its second pass) for the same underlying reason: the chair's own literal floor sits deep in the small-window overfitting regime for this car's real kappa/Fx noise.
longitudinal_stiffness.max_window_m_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_ls_max_window_locality_sizing.py, 2026-09-19, mirroring modules.stability_analysis's own cs_max_window_m REVISION methodology (natural uncapped window footprint under the just-derived floors, real track distance via s_m, longitudinal-DEMAND samples only). Measured footprint (both sessions, both axles): Dubai front median=61.6m/p90=424.6m/p95=556.7m/p99=830.7m, Dubai rear median=24.5m/p90=171.9m/p95=345.7m/p99=586.0m, v3 front median=111.0m/p90=609.9m/p95=840.2m/p99=1122.0m (the most demanding case throughout), v3 rear median=37.9m/p90=254.0m/p95=447.0m/p99=727.8m. DEVIATION FROM CS's OWN MULTIPLIER, stated not hidden: CS sized its cap at 1.5x its own more-demanding-axle MEDIAN, because CS's own median/p90 ratio was tight (~3x, a naturally compact lateral-cornering footprint). LS's own footprint is far more heavy-tailed (v3 front median/p90 ratio ~5.5x) -- a REAL, physical difference: LS's own domain is longitudinal braking/traction zones, which can legitimately span a much longer track distance at speed than a single corner's lateral extent, not an estimator defect. Applying CS's literal 1.5x-median multiplier here (167m) would have sat BELOW even the p90 of the most demanding case, discarding a much larger share of genuine long-braking-zone signal than CS's own choice ever did to its own data. Sized instead at the P95 mark of the single most demanding case (v3 front, 840.2m), rounded to 900m -- comfortably captures routine real long-braking-zone events, sits clearly below the P99/max multi-event-spanning tail (1122.0m / 5696.9m) that a straight/no-real-signal stretch under a loose |ax|>1.0 demand mask can produce.
longitudinal_stiffness.plausibility_kappa_bound_note: Decided 2026-08-30 (user decision), from the kerb-strike wheel-speed spike investigation. Same value as that investigation's gap-selected ANOMALY_THRESHOLD: the non-kerb-masked racing population's own |kappa_wheel| p99.9 (11.444%), rounded up to 12.0% -- everything above it is rarer than 1-in-1000 among samples the kerb mask does not already flag. Tier B, data-derived from this session's own distribution, not a chair value (no chair equivalent exists). Used ONLY in combination with az-coincidence (modules/longitudinal_stiffness.py _apply_plausibility_guard) -- NEVER applied to kappa alone, see that function's own docstring for why.
longitudinal_stiffness.plausibility_az_window_note: Decided 2026-08-30 (user decision). Trailing (backward-looking) window, per axle, over which _apply_plausibility_guard checks for a recent kerb-like az disturbance before excluding an implausible-kappa sample. Sized from the measured post-kerb-event settle-time distribution (all 57 racing kerb events, not just a sample): rear (rl+rr) settle p50=160ms p75=560ms -- 0.6s sits just above p75, covering most rear ringdown without reaching into the multi-second tail (p90=2.1s, 2 events never settled within 3s); front (fl+fr) settle p50=0ms p90=396ms -- 0.15s is a conservative user-selected value above the near-zero median, ahead of the visible tail. These are user-chosen working values informed by that distribution, not a formulaic percentile pick -- re-derive if the underlying kerb-event population changes materially (new track, different kerb geometry).

wheel_speed_guard._comment: Wheel-speed plausibility gate (_guarded_wheel_speed_kmh), signal processing only. Per window_s window a log_speed_{corner} is invalid if std < std_min_kmh while moving (stuck) or its mean ratio to the axle mate is off 1.0 by more than ratio_max_deviation (ecu_speed decides which side). Invalid -> abs_speed_{corner} if available, else NaN. Trigger case: v3 log_speed_rr, spurious 300.5 kph peak, > 15% off its mate on 5.9% of moving samples (diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py). Feeds kappa and the LS guard.
wheel_speed_guard.window_s_note: Physical window duration, rate-derived to samples at runtime (same pattern as stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s) -- not independently re-derived this session, chosen as a plausible sub-second fault-detection window matching this project's other window-based guards (NIS gate 0.4s, kerb az windows 0.15-0.6s).
wheel_speed_guard.std_min_kmh_note: Stuck-while-moving floor. FIRST VALUE TRIED (1.0 kph) WAS WRONG, caught empirically before shipping (diagnostics/inspect_wheel_speed_guard_before_after.py's own first run flagged 22-45% of samples on every corner of BOTH sessions, including Dubai's known-healthy channels -- traced to this threshold, not the ratio check, which independently measured only 0.19% false-positive on the same Dubai FL/FR pair): a 0.5s window's real, healthy std is itself often below 1.6 kph (Dubai log_speed_fl, moving windows: p10=0.53, p25=0.91, p50=1.61 kph) -- 1.0 kph sat in the middle of NORMAL variation, not below it. 0.1 kph sits ~5x below that real p10, a genuine margin above true zero-variance rather than a guess -- the ratio-to-mate check is what actually catches real faults (v3's log_speed_rr); this stuck check is a rarely-firing defensive second condition, evaluated only on moving samples so genuine standstill is never mistaken for a stuck sensor.
wheel_speed_guard.ratio_max_deviation_derived_from: Gap-selected against v3's own log_speed_rr/log_speed_rl ratio-deviation distribution (moving samples, diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py): the real/plausible population sits below its own p90 (4.62% deviation -- ordinary cross-axle cornering differential and sensor noise), the fault population's own p95 is already 20.40% -- 10% sits in the gap between the two, well clear of both.
wheel_speed_guard.abs_speed_channel_note: abs_speed_fl/fr/rl/rr (config/channels.json, newly whitelisted this phase) are the ABS-domain wheel-speed alternative -- present and 100Hz on BOTH real sessions (v3 unit 'kph', Dubai unit 'mph', confirmed directly per file, same per-file-unit hazard as log_susp_travel/lap_distance -- modules.longitudinal_forces._normalize_wheel_speed_to_kmh converts, never assumes).

wheel_loads._comment: Per-wheel Fz from pushrod force and suspension travel (wheel_loads.py; Segers ch. 9/10). Level 4 per corner where log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are both valid; static split (Level 1) as fallback per corner, never a whole-session switch.
wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_note: Level 1 default (zero). log_dms_dam_* is already logged in [N] (confirmed from the raw file header, not assumed), so an offset here is a zero-load calibration correction the team would enter after a static gauge check, not a unit conversion. No such session-entered value exists yet anywhere in this project (no UI field, no setup_data key) -- left at 0.0 (i.e. the raw channel is trusted as already zeroed) until a real calibration procedure and entry point exist. The straight-line total-load validation is the check on whether 0.0 is a reasonable assumption for this file. [2026-10-03: an event whose gauges were zeroed against another reference (NBR) is handled upstream by channels.json event_zero_entries, before the range gate; this offset stays the static gauge-check calibration and stays 0.0.]
wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_note: Level 1, work-order-supplied figures (not independently sourced this package) -- per-wheel unsprung mass (upright, hub, brake, wheel/tyre assembly, half-shaft share), typical order of magnitude for a GT3-class car. Feeds the unsprung-mass lateral-transfer term, which bypasses the damper/spring entirely (reacts through the upright/tyre contact directly) and must be added on top of the damper-derived sprung force, never folded into it.
wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE, not a measured dynamic (loaded) radius. Derived from the team-supplied STATIC tyre circumference (front 2140mm / rear 2210mm, itself flagged TODO-verify, no datasheet seen) via radius = circumference/(2*pi): front 2140/(2*pi)=340.6mm, rear 2210/(2*pi)=351.8mm. Dynamic (loaded, rolling) radius is normally a few percent smaller than static/free radius under load -- this approximation is NOT corrected for that effect. Used only for the unsprung-mass transfer arm h_u; listed here explicitly as an estimate needing a better source.
wheel_loads.roll_centre_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE. Read from config/car_data.json kinematic_variants_front/rear's own stated baseline_variant (FS15 front, RS25 rear) roll_center_mm column, converted mm->m -- NOT confirmed against which kinematic variant is actually fitted for the GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 session (no setup record identifies it). Used for the sprung-mass GEOMETRIC lateral-transfer term (the portion of roll-induced load transfer carried through the suspension linkage/roll axis rather than through spring compression) -- this is the only sprung-mass transfer component added on top of the damper-derived force; the ELASTIC portion is already present in the measured pushrod force itself and must not be added twice.
wheel_loads.arb_motion_ratio_approximation_note: Work-order-authorised approximation: no dedicated ARB-linkage motion ratio is digitised anywhere in car_data.json (only 'N/mm at drop link' rate tables plus a scalar ratio_to_wheel). modules/wheel_loads.py approximates the ARB's own travel-to-wheel motion ratio with the SAME damper motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel value used for the pushrod force at that instant (axle-matched) -- an approximation, not a measured ARB kinematic curve, flagged per corner in the module's own docstring.
wheel_loads.arb_position_fallback_note: Level 1 fallback ARB blade position (1-7) used only when no per-corner session setup value (setup_parameters arb_fl/fr/rl/rr) is available for the file being analysed -- GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt carries no setup-sheet record. 4 sits inside setup_parameters.json arb_fl's own recorded typical_window (3-5), a reasonable mid-stiffness assumption, not a measurement of this session's actual ARB setting.
wheel_loads.bump_rubber_note: NEGLECTED (documented limitation, not modelled). No bump-rubber engagement detection or force contribution is included in this estimator -- a wheel deep enough into bump to contact its bump rubber will read an UNDER-estimated load (the rubber's own reaction force is invisible to this decomposition, only the main spring/damper and ARB paths are modelled). config/car_data.json's own bump_stop_curve (cellasto_20mm_40shore) exists but is not consumed here; a future upgrade could use log_susp_travel_* proximity to the bump-stop engagement point to flag (not correct) affected samples.
wheel_loads.aero_front_fraction_note: Level 1 estimate, car-specific but still not a real aero-balance measurement (windtunnel/CFD) -- UPDATED 2026-09-19 (rear axle-total residual decomposition). Front/rear split of modules.wheel_loads.estimate_session_corrected_axle_totals's own session-fitted aero coefficient c_session (a per-session MEASUREMENT, Level 2 -- this split fraction is the only unsourced part of that correction). SUPERSEDES 0.40 (2026-08-xx, an unmeasured GT3-typical rear-biased assumption, front/rear never actually fit for this car). 0.25 is derived from real per-corner damper data on v3 (all four corners damper-measured since 2026-09-18): fitting residual_N = a + b*v^2 independently per corner on straight-line (|ax|,|ay|<0.5) samples gives b_fl=0.178, b_fr=0.214, b_rl=0.604, b_rr=0.573 N/(m/s)^2 (R^2 0.56/0.61/0.91/0.91) -- front_b=0.392, rear_b=1.177, front fraction = 0.392/(0.392+1.177) = 0.25. Cross-session confirmed: Dubai's own independently-fit RL b=0.611 matches v3's RL b=0.604 almost exactly, on a different session with a different straight-line speed range -- the v^2 slope, and therefore this split, is not a single-session fitting artefact. Structural check performed before trusting this at all: modules.wheel_loads's own left/right roll-transfer terms cancel exactly in an axle's total (verified at +0.00 N both axles, both sessions) and axle-total residual correlation with |ay| is null (+0.031/-0.058) -- the v^2 fit this split comes from is not contaminated by a roll/geometric-transfer effect. Single-car, two-session telemetry evidence only, not a substitute for a real aero-balance figure -- still open with the team for confirmation against real windtunnel/CFD data. Every wheel_loads reconstruction result that used this split states the value in its own returned dict (aero_front_fraction key).
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_travel_mm_derived_f: 2026-09-03: Sample_Dubai.txt's log_susp_travel_rr found frozen (std=0.101mm, range=3.03mm over the whole session) vs its own axle-mate log_susp_travel_rl (std=5.39mm) and every other travel channel checked on both real sessions (Dubai fl/fr/rl: 5.13/6.52/5.39mm; GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 fl/fr/rl/rr: 4.88/7.01/7.20/4.87mm) -- a real dead/disconnected sensor, not a quiet corner (this file's own log_dms_dam_rr force channel is NOT frozen, std=2031N, so the wheel itself is moving, only its travel POT is not). 1.0mm sits with wide margin above the frozen channel (~10x) and well below every real channel's own std (~5x), a gap-selected floor in the same style as this project's other frozen-value guards.
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_force_N_derived_fro: 2026-09-03. No real frozen damper-force example has been observed yet (every log_dms_dam_* channel checked on both real sessions reads std 1489-2083N) -- this floor is set conservatively low (roughly 30-40x below the smallest real std seen) so it cannot false-flag a genuine but quiet corner, pending a real frozen-force case to calibrate against directly the way the travel floor above was. Same guard purpose: a channel logged 'valid' quality and sitting at a plausible constant value is still dead, and channel_quality_gates' own range check cannot see that (it checks the VALUE, not whether it varies).

corner_trace_display._comment: Plot-only: how far the corner trace window extends beyond the phase bracket, for approach and coast-out context. Clamped at the lap's own s range. Phase bands still cover the five phases only.
corner_trace_display.cs_ls_panel_y_range_note: Fixed y-range shared by the CS ratio and LS ratio panels in ui/views/corner_trace_dialog.py -- both are the same 1/0/negative scale, but LS_ratio's occasional numerically-unstable windows (a known finding) would otherwise force auto-range so wide the meaningful 0..1 region collapses. Data-derived from CS_ratio's own observed range on Dubai at the production kinematic config (min -3.065 rear / -1.872 front, checked 2026-09-01) plus headroom. Display-only clip, out-of-range samples simply not drawn -- pending the open decision on LS_ratio's numerical stability, which may supersede this.
corner_trace_display.ls_display_min_ax_mps2_note: Added 2026-09-01. Display-only mask: the corner-trace LS panel only draws a sample where |ax_mps2| exceeds this bound -- LS_ratio is a longitudinal-stiffness ratio and reads as noise, not signal, while the car is near-constant-speed (cruise/apex-coast), independent of the numerical-instability finding. Value chosen from this session's own |ax_mps2| distribution over the same base racing population as the LS_ratio statistics (moving & ~kerb & valid-lap racing time, n=24183): p5=0.474, p10=0.947, p20=1.807, median=3.970 m/s^2 -- this track's laps spend most of their time under real braking/traction demand, so even a modest cutoff excludes only the genuinely flat segments. 1.0 m/s^2 (~0.1g) is the standard vehicle-dynamics rule-of-thumb for negligible longitudinal load transfer, sits just above the p10 point of this distribution, and leaves the great majority (89.4%) of racing-time samples display-eligible (still subject to LS_ratio's own finite/masking gates on top). Tier C, no estimator/threshold change -- LS_ratio's own numeric output is untouched, only what the corner-trace panel draws.
corner_trace_display.default_laps_shown_note: NEW, additive (trace-dialog addendum item 2, 2026-09-01). Corner trace default: when opened from an 'All laps' analysis (a single-lap analysis still defaults to just that lap, unchanged), the fastest N valid laps of this corner start CHECKED, the rest start unchecked but available -- avoids a wall of overlapping colours on a corner with many laps by default while never refusing to show more if the user checks them. N=5 chosen as a readable default under the addendum's own 10-colour palette (comfortably below the point where the dash-cycling fallback would ever trigger). Tier C UI default, not a science/analysis parameter.
corner_trace_display.kerb_gap_bridge_derived_from: display continuity only, 2026-09-30. Corner and lap trace windows draw a dashed, lighter linear bridge across NaN runs that contain kerb-flagged samples (CS_ratio f/r and stability panels); plot code path only, no analysis array reads or receives it.
corner_trace_display.kerb_exclusion_display_note: Kerb exclusion, ONE user-facing concept (author rulings 2026-10-05, key renamed from near_strike_display 2026-10-07). Plot-only switch for every CS trace, histogram and tyre-curve scatter in the trace dialogs, the figure exports and the diagnostics renders, so app and thesis figures agree: grey (default) = kerb-affected samples drawn grey (hollow in the tyre-curve scatter); exclude = left out of the plot; off = drawn like every other sample. Every view states one caption with the count. Kerb-affected = inside the kerb mask or carrying the estimator's grade mark (internal name near_strike, width stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s). Presentation only: the estimator deletes nothing and no computed result changes (no schema bump).

cs_envelope._comment: Corner-trace cross-lap envelope (core/trace_display.cross_lap_envelope), drawn as two thin lines on the CS front / CS rear / stability panels over ALL analysis laps of the corner; the selected lap full-strength on top. Display only.
cs_envelope.percentiles_derived_from: Author ruling 2026-10-06 (app check): p10 / p90 rather than min / max -- one wild lap must not set the visual band.
cs_envelope.min_laps_derived_from: Same floor as yaw_pooling.min_laps: fewer laps at a grid point -> no band there.

corner_trace_display.yaw_pooling_panel_derived_from: (c)-display, approved 2026-09-30, display continuity with diagnostic inspect_yaw_pooling. Corner and lap trace windows add a yaw-rate panel (per-lap yaw rate on a 1 m grid, pooled median, envelope, excess/deficit flag overlays) and a steering-rate sub-panel. Display only: no estimator, threshold, classification or evidence reads it. Read when the trace windows are built.

yaw_pooling._comment: Tier B values for core/yaw_pooling.build_panel_data (author ruling 2026-09-30: config, each tied to the diagnostic's pre-registration; the diagnostic keeps its own constants). Changing one changes the display only.
yaw_pooling.lowpass_hz_derived_from: Pre-registered in diagnostics/inspect_yaw_pooling.py header ((c) Part 1, 2026-09-30); display continuity with that diagnostic. Zero-phase low-pass of yaw rate and steering angle: removes vibration spikes, keeps 0.1 s-scale rotation.
yaw_pooling.noise_trend_hz_derived_from: Pre-registered in diagnostics/inspect_yaw_pooling.py header ((c) Part 1, 2026-09-30); display continuity with that diagnostic. Trend removed before the straight-line noise std, so slow heading changes on straights do not count as noise.
yaw_pooling.grid_m_derived_from: Pre-registered in diagnostics/inspect_yaw_pooling.py header ((c) Part 1, 2026-09-30); display continuity with that diagnostic. Track-position resampling step for cross-lap comparison.

stab_neg_thresh_Nm_per_deg.derived_from: 2026-10-05, author ruling: Werner 2021 sec. 2.2.3 sign criterion as the anchored boundary -- dMz/dbeta < 0 is open-loop unstable; explicitly not a criticality threshold (skilled drivers operate there), so the verdict reads 'open-loop unstable (Werner)' and its severity stays contextual (two-signal logic). Measure chair-conform (inertial regressand, default (c)). Clean-pool worst-phase distribution beside (inspect_threshold_rederivation.py counts_clean): n 109, 9 negative, p5 -5 / p10 +27 / p15 +50 Nm/deg. Supersedes -50.0 (2026-07-24, kinematic-era placeholder, never re-derived for ekf_auto_pacejka), retired 2026-10-05. [2026-10-06: the product text reads 'open-loop unstable' -- no source names in the app (author ruling); the anchor stays here and in PRODUCTION.md.]

verdict_stability_margin.derived_from: 2026-09-19, verdict sensitivity sweep (diagnostics/inspect_metrology_phase1_sensitivity.py). Not a threshold -- a MARGINAL annotation ui/views/outing_form.py's _classify_corner appends to its own verdict when the axle value actually driving that verdict sits within cs_margin of the nearest STRONG/MODERATE_CS* threshold. 0.11 is the empirical threshold-distance of the 2nd-most-marginal corner-phase that actually flipped under a real +/-1% perturbation of mass/front_fraction/wheelbase/yaw_inertia/steering_ratio (v3 C12 apex_3/exit_4, distance 0.104, rounded up slightly), covering 9 of the 10 observed flips. The one excluded case (Dubai C1 apex_3, distance 0.274) was read directly and found to be a different mechanism (which of CSf/CSr is currently more extreme, a relative front/rear comparison _classify_corner also makes, not a fixed-threshold crossing) -- inflating this margin to cover it would flag far more corners than the sweep supports. TWO-SESSION CAVEAT, stated not hidden: this anchor is derived from exactly two real sessions (Dubai, GT3_PRC_MLA-v3) -- re-check it once a third session's own sensitivity sweep is available, the same standing caveat every single/two-session-derived threshold in this block already carries (STRONG/MODERATE_CSF/CSR above are also single-session). [2026-10-05: re-measured on the corrected chain, wheel-angle-column sweep (diagnostics/inspect_metrology_phase1_sensitivity.py adapted: the steering input now perturbs the table's wheel-angle column +/-1 % instead of the ratio column, which production no longer reads; results in diagnostics/results_metrology_20261005/): no proportional flip within +/-1 %; both flips are different-mechanism jumps per the recorded exclusions (v3 C8 exit_4 ratio discontinuity, Dubai C1 apex_3); value retained. Author ruling 2026-10-05.] [2026-10-11: re-measured on the corrected estimator and the 2026-10-11 thresholds, same 22-run +/-1 % sweep (diagnostics/inspect_metrology_phase1_sensitivity.py with METROLOGY_RUN_TAG=20261011, results in diagnostics/results_metrology_20261011/): 0 corner-phase flips across 5 inputs x 2 directions x 2 sessions, although 13 of 232 corner-phase values sit within 0.11 of a threshold (closest 0.001, v3 C16 exit_4 front). The derivation rule needs a proportional flip; with none, no new value follows -- value retained, as on 2026-10-05.]

limit_events._comment: Limit events (modules/limit_events.py): in-corner stretches where CS lies below the session's own 0-30 deg curve floor, per axle -- display + record only, never a verdict or recommendation input. Merge and recurrence values are the Q-SPIKE-AUDIT frozen ones; the event line itself is computed from the session's fit, not configured.
limit_events.bridge_gap_s_derived_from: Q-SPIKE-AUDIT frozen header (diagnostics/inspect_spike_audit.py BRIDGE_S, 2026-10-05): sub-threshold gaps shorter than this merge two stretches into one event. Author ruling 2026-10-06: the only merge logic.
limit_events.recurrence_radius_m_derived_from: Q-SPIKE-AUDIT frozen header (SITE_M, the Q-PAIRING radius, 2026-10-05): an event recurs when another analysis lap has an event of the same axle at the same corner with its minimum within this lap distance.
limit_events.min_duration_s_derived_from: One CS regression window (stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s), the estimator's own resolution: an event cannot be shorter than the shortest window that produced its values; sub-window excursions are numerical edges, not observations. Ruled 2026-10-06 (author) on the first real counts (single-sample events 9 of 49 on Dubai, 11 of 91 on NBR JST 29). Not a transferred surface-noise rule (Segers sec. 7.4 is for raw lateral g). Compared with a half-sample tolerance so an event of exactly one window is kept.

accuracy_levels._comment: Accuracy per quantity: 1 = config default, 2 = session measurement, 3 = logged sensor, 4 = lookup table. Per node: level (static default tier), source, capped_by ('chained-constant: <name>' = an L1 constant in its derivation; 'provenance-assumption: <name>' = an unverifiable assumption about the channel; null = neither). accuracy_resolution.py resolves leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, steering_ratio) per outing; derived nodes cascade from capped_by -- pure (= input level) or bounded by method_ceiling (e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b). Other nodes stay at their static level regardless of cap.

yaw_inertia_kalman.note: Diagnostics-only Kalman sideslip observer candidate (diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py); not consumed by any production Module 2-6 path. Distinct node from yaw_inertia (production, vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2) -- deliberately not chained to it.

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); dynamically resolves to Level 4 (car_data.json steering_ratio_table, manufacturer digitised) when that local-only file is present and the cap allows it -- modules/accuracy_resolution.py. At Level 4 the wheel angle is interpolated from the table's wheel-angle column (mean of both front wheels), not divided by its ratio column, which is the local slope (corrected 2026-10-04, schema 10). Parameterization, not a chair-comparison deviation: the constant was never a chair scientific position, it is this car's own mechanical steering geometry.

longitudinal_force_split.source: Fx_f/Fx_r fallback tier: m*ax + drag + rolling, split by measured brake pressure / rear-drive assumption (estimate_longitudinal_forces), chair-identical construction (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py, internal)
longitudinal_force_split.note: 2026-08-30. drag_coeff/rolling_resistance_coeff are both 0.0 placeholders (longitudinal_stiffness namespace) -- Fx currently reduces to m*ax plus the measured brake-pressure split, no resistive-force correction yet.

sideslip_angle.source: per-session EKF/Pacejka auto-fit, gated (modules/tyre_fit_auto.resolve_sideslip_beta, stability_estimation.sideslip_source='ekf_auto_pacejka', production default since 2026-09-01), falling back to kinematic integration + washout (estimate_sideslip) whenever modules/nis_gate.py verdicts 'fail' or the fit is 'degenerate'
sideslip_angle.note: GPS-course L3 path investigated (two iterations, 2026-07-26): NOT viable on this dataset - diagnosed scale-drift corrected and corroborated, remaining error not dominated by it; shelved pending denser anchor data (longer session / more straights). Still Level 1: the auto-fit is a per-session model fit, not a higher-tier measured/logged/lookup source: fallback path and gate outcome are recorded in the analysis payload (fallback_used/fallback_reason), never silent.

speed.capped_by: provenance-assumption: opaque ECU wheel-speed calibration (thesis_notes.md limitations register item 10)
speed.note: GPS speed cross-validation investigated (2026-07-26): diagnostic/validation only, NOT switched to production -- ecu_speed remains the production source and pipeline time-anchor throughout. Measured a consistent origin-regression scale factor k=1.012 (ecu_speed reads ~1.2% low vs GPS, tight across speed classes, braking/traction slip prediction NOT confirmed as the dominant driver of the offset) -- a candidate rolling-radius correction to ecu_speed's own conversion. MEASURING k is not itself an estimator-input change; APPLYING it would be (v feeds Modules 2-5 and the aero-Fz term), and is a separate future decision with its own re-derivation stop, not taken here.

yaw_rate.source: sclu_yaw_rate logged channel, exact rpm-to-radps unit conversion

steering_angle.source: log_asteer logged channel (steering-wheel angle), converted via the constant steering_ratio at Level 1 or the manufacturer wheel-angle map at Level 4 (pure cascade -- resolves to steering_ratio's own resolved level)

lateral_acc.source: log_acc_y logged channel, exact g-to-mps2 unit conversion

wheelbase_m.note: Fixed chassis dimension, known to design tolerance; not expected to move enough to justify a dedicated remeasurement -- kept at Level 1 by convention, not as a live upgrade target.

vertical_load_split.source: axle Fz static + aero + longitudinal-transfer decomposition (estimate_vertical_loads), chair-identical construction (docs/literature/data_handler.py, internal)

per_wheel_load_split.source: per-axle independent lateral-transfer split (estimate_vertical_loads), the chair's own construction (docs/literature/data_handler.py, internal) -- NOT the roll-stiffness apportionment scoped as a later DOMAIN IMPROVEMENT
per_wheel_load_split.note: 2026-07-26. [2026-10-03: this level describes the STATIC split only. With vertical_load_source = measured the level is per sample (vertical_load_source_per_sample): 'damper' = L4 (logged sensor + motion-ratio table); on NBR the damper channels carry an event zero entry (channels.json event_zero_entries), so NBR damper loads are 'L4 with an L2 zero' (L4-rel, author ruling, Q-CAL-2).]

wheel_load_damper.source: damper/pushrod force + motion ratio + ARB + unsprung/geometric lateral-transfer decomposition (modules/wheel_loads.py), per corner, when log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are both valid for that corner -- Segers ch. 9/10 method
wheel_load_damper.capped_by: chained-constant: wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_front/rear_kg, wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.roll_centre_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, car_data.json motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel/arb tables
wheel_load_damper.note: 2026-09-02. Per-CORNER, not per-session: a corner whose damper or travel channel is missing/failed (e.g. GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt's own faulted log_dms_dam_fr) falls back to per_wheel_load_split's Level 1 static estimate for that corner alone, recorded per-sample, never a silent session-wide substitution. Not yet wired into modules/accuracy_resolution.py's dynamic per-session cascade or any UI/pipeline consumer .

wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.source: quasi-static heave/pitch axle-total (vertical_load_split's own fz_f_N/fz_r_N) minus the real damper-measured axle-mate (modules/wheel_loads.py reconstruct_missing_corner), used ONLY where exactly one corner of an axle is damper-invalid and its mate is damper-valid -- Segers modal-decomposition method
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.capped_by: chained-constant: vertical_load_split (cog_height_m, aero lift_coeff/cross_track_area_m2/diff_cog_x_m -- the axle-total half of this method), wheel_load_damper (the measured-mate half)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.note: 2026-09-03. Deliberately registered at the SAME nominal Level 1 as per_wheel_load_split despite using three real sensors -- the accuracy-level system records provenance TIER (what kind of source), not within-tier confidence, and this method's own axle-total term is capped by the same unsourced Level-1 aero/cog-height placeholders per_wheel_load_split already carries. In practice more accurate than a pure static-split guess for the missing corner (it uses a real measurement for 3 of the 4 unknowns instead of 0), but that is a within-Level-1 distinction this registry does not represent numerically. Cascade position: tried AFTER wheel_load_damper (Level 4, that corner's own sensor), BEFORE per_wheel_load_split (Level 1 static-only fallback) -- modules.wheel_loads.combine_with_reconstruction_and_fallback implements the three-tier order. LIMITATIONS (full detail in reconstruct_missing_corner's own docstring): a single-wheel event unique to the reconstructed corner is invisible (the axle-total model has no road-input sensing); the warp/torsion mode ((FL+RR)-(FR+RL)) is unobservable with three sensors and a heave/pitch-only model; both corners of the same axle invalid at once falls through to per_wheel_load_split instead (no reconstruction possible from one equation with two unknowns).

yaw_damping.source: D_psi = (C_alpha_f*l_f^2 + C_alpha_r*l_r^2)/v (modules/yaw_damping.py), with the effective stiffnesses taken from Module 4b's model-free measured local slopes (C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r), not from a tyre model -- no wheel load enters
yaw_damping.note: 2026-09-29. Weakest link of its inputs: C_alpha is Level 1 (Fy from the Level-1 force split, alpha from the Level-1 sideslip chain), l_f/l_r follow cog_position (Level 2 with a session weighing), v is speed (Level 1), psi_dot is yaw_rate (Level 3). NaN wherever either axle's stiffness is invalid or v is at/below moving_speed_min_mps; negative stiffness passes through as negative damping. Diagnostic consumer only -- not in Module 5, the payload or the UI.
yaw_damping.derived_from: Werner 2021 sec. 4.5.2 (Eqs. 4.3/4.4) and Milliken RCVD ch. 5 (sec. 5.7, Eq. 5.6); effective stiffness from logged Fy/alpha (Module 4b) instead of a tyre model, approved 2026-09-29.
